note: Controls for tools/cutover, the one-time v6-to-v7 conversion dw32p.28 runs once per machine. The clauses are the decisions the conversion cannot derive from the data: which key each Project takes, which remote is a locator, what happens to each memory, what the outcome must be, and what is proved before anything is written. Seeded by dw32p.28.

controls.clause: Two machines converting their own store independently derive the same key for a slug, so the Projects they both hold are one Project after sync (dw32p.28)
A derived key is 128 bits Base32-encoded, which is the only shape model.ParseProjectKey accepts (dw32p.28)
global and inbox take model's fixed keys, so deriving one would put a second spelling of a pinned identity in the tree (dw32p.7)
The plan's slug table omits the reserved slugs, which projectKeys.forSlug pins before it consults the plan (dw32p.28)
A filesystem path cleans to exactly the shape of host/owner/repo, so the host segment must look like a host (dw32p.21)
git@host:owner/repo is not a URL, so its colon becomes the path separator before anything parses it (dw32p.8)
The user part of git@host:path is not part of the repository's identity (dw32p.8)
The same repository reached as .git and without it is one locator (dw32p.8)
Host case is not part of a repository's identity, while path case is (dw32p.8)
An unnormalizable remote is reported as skipped by the conversion rather than guessed at (dw32p.28)
The 31 memories dw32p.11 omits do not migrate
Ownership is semantic: a subject-specific row filed globally moves to the Project it describes (dw32p.11)
A legacy memory with no project lands in the reserved global Project (dw32p.11)
v7 drops the kind column, so the kind survives as searchable prose or stops being searchable (dw32p.9)
v7 omission is not a tombstone, so carrying a deleted row across resurrects it rather than migrating its deletion (dw32p.28)
No legacy supersession edge beyond the eight dw32p.11 named is written
A supersession into a dropped row makes the conversion refuse, and an unmeasured memory did not make that judgement (dw32p.28)
An explicit parent-child edge is authoritative, so its child is not also inferred from its spelling (dw32p.12)
A dotted spelling naming no existing Issue is not parentage evidence (dw32p.12)
A dotted-only pair is retained when child and parent share a Project (dw32p.12)
A cross-Project dotted-only pair is omitted only when its child is tombstoned; a live one refuses migration (dw32p.12)
The conversion refuses a store whose parentage the rule will not choose between, before it writes anything (dw32p.12)
v7 keeps parentage in its own table, so a parent-child edge is not also a dependency (dw32p.7)
v7 holds global and inbox whether or not v6 did, so the census counts them (dw32p.7)
The curation moves memories into Projects the legacy store never had, and the conversion creates them (dw32p.11)
The census is handed to Rewrite as Expect, so a conversion that disagrees with it commits nothing (dw32p.28)
Without the curation every legacy memory migrates, including the 31 dw32p.11 omits
The active replica key lives only in the sidecar, so a conversion that does not write one authors later writes under a key no converted record names as its origin (dw32p.10)
A rehearsal converts a throwaway copy, never the store it was pointed at (dw32p.28)
A restore is proved rather than trusted: the copy is reopened and re-counted before the conversion (AGENTS.md, dw32p.28)
Proving the backup means it holds what the store holds, not merely that it opens (dw32p.28)
The backup is the only other copy of the pre-cutover rows (dw32p.28)
The v7 transport writes into the same directory and its history commits a different file set, so the v6 mirror does not stay (dw32p.28)
